title: Korean Fried Chicken
subtitle: Double-fried chicken wings in a sticky gochujang glaze
excerpt: Korean fried chicken (yangnyeom chicken) is double-fried for an exceptionally thin, shatteringly crispy crust, then tossed in a sweet, spicy, and sticky gochujang glaze. The double-frying method renders out the fat from the skin on the first fry, then crisps it on the second at higher heat.
sourceNotes: Korean fried chicken (chikin) exploded in popularity in South Korea in the 1970s and 1980s, particularly as delivery food. The double-frying technique and the thin starchy coating distinguish Korean fried chicken from other styles. The yangnyeom (seasoned/spicy) version with gochujang glaze became the most popular internationally from the 2000s onwards.

content.text: The first fry is at a lower temperature (160°C) and cooks the chicken through without browning the coating much. The second fry at a higher temperature (180°C) crisps the skin in 2 to 3 minutes. The glaze goes on after the second fry. Add it just before serving or the crust softens quickly.

items.prepNote: tips removed, split at the joint

content.text: Make the glaze: combine the gochujang, honey, soy sauce, garlic, sesame oil, and rice vinegar in a small saucepan. Simmer for 3 minutes, stirring, until slightly thickened. Keep warm.

Mix the cornflour, plain flour, ground ginger, white pepper, and 1 teaspoon of salt. Pat the chicken wings dry with kitchen paper. Toss in the flour mixture until thoroughly coated. Shake off any excess.

Heat the oil to 160°C in a deep saucepan. Fry the wings in batches for 8 to 10 minutes until cooked through (no longer pink at the bone). Drain on a wire rack. Let the oil return to temperature between batches.
Increase the oil to 180°C. Return all the wings to the oil for 2 to 3 minutes until deeply golden and shatteringly crispy. Drain.
Toss the hot wings immediately in the glaze until well coated. Scatter with sesame seeds and serve at once.

items.cause: Wings were not dried before coating, or the coating was too thin
items.fix: Pat the wings completely dry with kitchen paper before coating. Press the flour mixture onto the wings firmly.
